title: ROOT: Exploit a memory-safety flaw in OBC firmware
text: Generic firmware memory-safety campaign. Objective: turn an unbounded copy in the on-board computer firmware into code execution. Steps: recover/inspect firmware, find an unbounded copy of external data, trigger the overflow with crafted input, gain control.
source: synthesized from SPARTA EX-0009 and firmware cases (BEESAT-1).

title: Recover and inspect the firmware
text: Sub-step. Obtain the firmware image and locate input-handling routines. Deterministic check: input parser routines identified in the image.

title: Find an unbounded copy of external data
text: Sub-step. Identify a memcpy/strcpy/sprintf where the length comes from untrusted input. Deterministic check: a copy with an unchecked external length is located.

title: Trigger the overflow with crafted input
text: Sub-step. Send an over-length input through the relevant interface to overflow the buffer. Deterministic check: a memory-safety oracle (sanitizer/crash) trips.

title: Gain control of execution
text: Sub-step. Use the corruption to redirect control flow and run attacker code. Deterministic check: attacker-controlled code executes.

title: ROOT: Inject an accepted command via the uplink
text: Generic telecommand-injection campaign. Objective: get an effecting command accepted by the spacecraft without authorization. Steps: establish an uplink, craft a valid-looking command, defeat or exploit absent authentication, confirm execution.

title: Establish an uplink to the command receiver
text: Sub-step. Transmit on the command band as a rogue ground station. Deterministic check: a frame is demodulated by the command receiver.

title: Craft a valid-looking command frame
text: Sub-step. Build a command frame conforming to the command format. Deterministic check: the frame passes the command parser.

title: Defeat or exploit absent command authentication
text: Sub-step. If authentication is missing the step is free; otherwise modify or bypass the authentication process. Deterministic check: an unauthenticated/forged command is not rejected.

title: Confirm the command executes
text: Sub-step. Verify the effecting handler runs. Deterministic check: a guarded action executes or a state invariant changes.

title: ROOT: Get a forged frame accepted by exploiting missing integrity checks
text: Generic protocol-integrity campaign. Objective: have a forged or replayed frame accepted because integrity/authentication is not enforced. Steps: analyze the protocol, forge or replay a frame, exploit the missing CRC/auth check.

title: Analyze the protocol framing
text: Sub-step. Recover the frame format and where integrity is supposed to be checked. Deterministic check: the frame format and integrity field are identified.

title: Forge or replay a frame
text: Sub-step. Build a frame with attacker content, or replay a captured one. Deterministic check: a forged/replayed frame is transmitted.

title: Exploit the missing CRC/authentication check
text: Sub-step. The receiver processes the frame despite a failed or absent integrity check. Deterministic check: a frame with bad/absent integrity is accepted.

title: ROOT: Compromise via a vulnerable third-party dependency
text: Generic supply-chain campaign. Objective: reach the spacecraft software through a flawed vendored dependency (e.g. an RTOS or library). Steps: enumerate dependencies, find a flaw in one, reach it through the integrating code.

title: Enumerate third-party dependencies
text: Sub-step. List vendored libraries, RTOS, and toolchain components. Deterministic check: a dependency inventory with versions is produced.

title: Find a flaw in a dependency
text: Sub-step. Identify a known or new weakness in a vendored component. Deterministic check: a flawed routine in a dependency is located.

title: Reach the flaw through integrating code
text: Sub-step. Confirm the application calls the flawed dependency path with attacker-influenced data. Deterministic check: a reachable call path to the flaw exists.

title: ROOT: Cause physical loss via a destructive attitude command (ROSAT-style)
text: Decomposition of the ROSAT-class outcome (see inc-rosat-1998). Objective: from a ground foothold, issue a command that drives the spacecraft to a destructive attitude. Steps: compromise the ground system, reach commanding, issue a destructive on-board value change. Attribution disputed; modeled as worst-case.

title: Compromise the ground system
text: Sub-step. Gain a foothold on the operations ground system. Deterministic check: session on a ground-control host.

title: Reach the commanding path
text: Sub-step. Act as a legitimate ground station to send commands. Deterministic check: commanding interface reachable.

title: Issue a destructive attitude command
text: Sub-step. Modify on-board values to slew optics toward the sun, causing irreversible damage. Deterministic check: an attitude-safety invariant (sun avoidance) is violated.

title: ROOT: Deny the command link by jamming
text: Decomposition of link jamming (see inc-gnss-satcom-jamming). Objective: deny service by flooding the receive band. Steps: obtain a transmitter, identify the band, jam the uplink.

title: Obtain a transmitter in the target band
text: Sub-step. Acquire an RF source capable of the uplink band and power. Deterministic check: a transmitter covering the band is available.

title: Identify the uplink band and timing
text: Sub-step. Determine the receive frequency and pass windows. Deterministic check: the uplink band/timing is characterized.

title: Jam the uplink
text: Sub-step. Flood the uplink band with noise during a pass so commands cannot be received. Deterministic check: the receiver fails to demodulate legitimate commands under the jammer.
